html:
The Poqomam are a Maya people of the highlands of Guatemala, living mainly around Guatemala City, in towns such as Mixco, Chinautla and Palín, and in Jalapa to the east. A few communities lived in western El Salvador. Their language is close to Poqomchi', spoken further north, and both belong to the Mayan family.

In 1492 they were one of many small Maya states and peoples of the highlands, alongside the larger K'iche' and Kaqchikel kingdoms. From 1524 the Spanish under Pedro de Alvarado conquered the region, and Poqomam towns were moved and regrouped under Spanish rule. Poqomam is still spoken today, though Spanish has replaced it in many homes.
